verdicts.justification: Reproduced exactly: load('sotus') returned "type: <class 'sklearn.pipeline.Pipeline'>" and hyp.plot(sotus) raised "TypeError Unsupported data type passed. Supported types: Numpy Array, Pandas DataFrame, String, List of strings, List of numbers". Root cause independently confirmed in the registry: hypertools/io/load.py line 24 "'sotus': '1J0MBhpRwdT2WChfWJ4HXYq6jU4XpyJPm'" and line 27 "'nips_model': '1J0MBhpRwdT2WChfWJ4HXYq6jU4XpyJPm'" -- identical Google Drive IDs -- and md5 of both cached files is 6a350ab8d85db34e7b924ac8a7f2a19b. load.py's own docstring (line 167) promises "`sotus` is a collection of State of the Union speeches from 1989-2018." Documented example dataset is entirely broken.

Reproduced: fig.axes[0].lines[0].get_data_3d() gives "F002 vertices: (900,)" for 10000-sample input; "true max coord: 53.88 drawn max coord: 1.0". To rule out mere normalization I measured outlier structure of the drawn line: max/99th-pct distance-from-median ratio of the 900 drawn points is 1.05 (no needle) vs 12.94 for identically-normalized ground truth -- the 50-sigma spike is dropped before scaling, not rescaled. Endpoint variant (+500 on last sample): last drawn point r=0.545 vs bulk max 1.83 -- endpoint spike also absent. Re-rendered PNGs (spike_hypertools_reverify.png vs spike_groundtruth_reverify.png) visually confirm: hypertools shows only the random-walk cloud, ground truth is dominated by the needle to (50,50,50). Silent lossy resampling of static plots producing a clearly-wrong visual: major is fair.

Reproduced exactly: "F003 static dur=30 fr=30 -> (900,)", "dur=60 fr=30 -> (1800,)", "dur=1 fr=2 -> (2,)" -- a 10000-sample static trajectory drawn as 2 vertices. plot() docstring lines 791 and 862 literally label these "duration (animation only)" and "frame_rate (animation only)", so their effect on static plots contradicts the documentation.

Reproduced: exported gif has "F006: n_frames=60 first_delay=30ms total=1.80s size=1.55MB" (all 60 frame delays summed = 1.80 s) for duration=2, frame_rate=30. animate.py lines 23-26 claim frames are written "at 1000/frame_rate ms each" so the file "plays in real time: ... total ~= duration seconds"; PillowWriter's GIF centisecond quantization makes 33.33 ms -> 30 ms, a systematic 10% fast playback at the default frame rate. Comment's specific '1000/frame_rate ms each' claim is factually wrong; doc severity is right.
